## 1. Chart type
- **Alluvial / Sankey-style flow chart** showing how total water consumption is divided into categories and subcategories.

## 2. Layout techniques
- Uses **flow bands** whose **width represents quantity/share**.
- Shows **hierarchical splitting** from a total into major categories, then into subcategories.
- No faceting or small multiples.
- Not stacked in the usual bar/area-chart sense; instead it uses **branching flows**.

## 3. Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Total water consumed (“1.9 trillion gallons of water”) | Quantitative | Overall total indicated by title text; implied by full combined flow area |
| Major water-use category (Livestock, Other crops, Everything else) | Categorical/nominal | Separate flow branches/segments; text labels |
| Subcategory within major category (Cotton, Wheat, Corn grain, Barley, Other crops, Thermoelectric power, Commercial and industrial, Residential) | Categorical/nominal | Nested flow branches; text labels |
| Share of total water use (percent values such as 56%, 24%, 21%, 12%, 7%, etc.) | Quantitative | Flow width/area; percentage labels |
| Water volume in gallons (e.g., 1,064 billion gallons; 448 billion gallons; 387 billion gallons) | Quantitative | Text labels for major categories |
| Hierarchical relationship / grouping (subcategory belonging to a major category) | Ordinal/structural grouping | Branching/nesting of flows from parent category |

## 1. Chart type
- **Alluvial / Sankey-style flow chart** showing how total water consumption is divided into categories and subcategories.

## 2. Layout techniques
- Uses **flow bands** whose **width represents quantity/share**.
- Shows **hierarchical splitting** from a total into major categories, then into subcategories.
- No faceting or small multiples.
- Not stacked in the usual bar/area-chart sense; instead it uses **branching flows**.

## 3. Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Total water consumed (“1.9 trillion gallons of water”) | Quantitative | Overall total indicated by title text; implied by full combined flow area |
| Major water-use category (Livestock, Other crops, Everything else) | Categorical/nominal | Separate flow branches/segments; text labels |
| Subcategory within major category (Cotton, Wheat, Corn grain, Barley, Other crops, Thermoelectric power, Commercial and industrial, Residential) | Categorical/nominal | Nested flow branches; text labels |
| Share of total water use (percent values such as 56%, 24%, 21%, 12%, 7%, etc.) | Quantitative | Flow width/area; percentage labels |
| Water volume in gallons (e.g., 1,064 billion gallons; 448 billion gallons; 387 billion gallons) | Quantitative | Text labels for major categories |
| Hierarchical relationship / grouping (subcategory belonging to a major category) | Ordinal/structural grouping | Branching/nesting of flows from parent category |

image_description:
## 1. Chart type
- **Alluvial / Sankey-style flow chart** showing how total water consumption is divided into categories and subcategories.

## 2. Layout techniques
- Uses **flow bands** whose **width represents quantity/share**.
- Shows **hierarchical splitting** from a total into major categories, then into subcategories.
- No faceting or small multiples.
- Not stacked in the usual bar/area-chart sense; instead it uses **branching flows**.

## 3. Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Total water consumed (“1.9 trillion gallons of water”) | Quantitative | Overall total indicated by title text; implied by full combined flow area |
| Major water-use category (Livestock, Other crops, Everything else) | Categorical/nominal | Separate flow branches/segments; text labels |
| Subcategory within major category (Cotton, Wheat, Corn grain, Barley, Other crops, Thermoelectric power, Commercial and industrial, Residential) | Categorical/nominal | Nested flow branches; text labels |
| Share of total water use (percent values such as 56%, 24%, 21%, 12%, 7%, etc.) | Quantitative | Flow width/area; percentage labels |
| Water volume in gallons (e.g., 1,064 billion gallons; 448 billion gallons; 387 billion gallons) | Quantitative | Text labels for major categories |
| Hierarchical relationship / grouping (subcategory belonging to a major category) | Ordinal/structural grouping | Branching/nesting of flows from parent category |

Corn is particularly relevant to my community, as it is one of the principal crops grown in Champaign County (along with soybeans).

image_description:
## 1. Chart type
- **Alluvial / Sankey-style flow chart** showing how total water consumption is divided into categories and subcategories.

## 2. Layout techniques
- Uses **flow bands** whose **width represents quantity/share**.
- Shows **hierarchical splitting** from a total into major categories, then into subcategories.
- No faceting or small multiples.
- Not stacked in the usual bar/area-chart sense; instead it uses **branching flows**.

## 3. Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Total water consumed (“1.9 trillion gallons of water”) | Quantitative | Overall total indicated by title text; implied by full combined flow area |
| Major water-use category (Livestock, Other crops, Everything else) | Categorical/nominal | Separate flow branches/segments; text labels |
| Subcategory within major category (Cotton, Wheat, Corn grain, Barley, Other crops, Thermoelectric power, Commercial and industrial, Residential) | Categorical/nominal | Nested flow branches; text labels |
| Share of total water use (percent values such as 56%, 24%, 21%, 12%, 7%, etc.) | Quantitative | Flow width/area; percentage labels |
| Water volume in gallons (e.g., 1,064 billion gallons; 448 billion gallons; 387 billion gallons) | Quantitative | Text labels for major categories |
| Hierarchical relationship / grouping (subcategory belonging to a major category) | Ordinal/structural grouping | Branching/nesting of flows from parent category |

We could install more desalinization plants in the US to try and compensate for the lack of fresh water we have left. ## 1. Chart type
- **Alluvial / Sankey-style flow chart** showing how total water consumption is divided into categories and subcategories.

## 2. Layout techniques
- Uses **flow bands** whose **width represents quantity/share**.
- Shows **hierarchical splitting** from a total into major categories, then into subcategories.
- No faceting or small multiples.
- Not stacked in the usual bar/area-chart sense; instead it uses **branching flows**.

## 3. Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Total water consumed (“1.9 trillion gallons of water”) | Quantitative | Overall total indicated by title text; implied by full combined flow area |
| Major water-use category (Livestock, Other crops, Everything else) | Categorical/nominal | Separate flow branches/segments; text labels |
| Subcategory within major category (Cotton, Wheat, Corn grain, Barley, Other crops, Thermoelectric power, Commercial and industrial, Residential) | Categorical/nominal | Nested flow branches; text labels |
| Share of total water use (percent values such as 56%, 24%, 21%, 12%, 7%, etc.) | Quantitative | Flow width/area; percentage labels |
| Water volume in gallons (e.g., 1,064 billion gallons; 448 billion gallons; 387 billion gallons) | Quantitative | Text labels for major categories |
| Hierarchical relationship / grouping (subcategory belonging to a major category) | Ordinal/structural grouping | Branching/nesting of flows from parent category |

image_description:
## 1. Chart type
- **Alluvial / Sankey-style flow chart** showing how total water consumption is divided into categories and subcategories.

## 2. Layout techniques
- Uses **flow bands** whose **width represents quantity/share**.
- Shows **hierarchical splitting** from a total into major categories, then into subcategories.
- No faceting or small multiples.
- Not stacked in the usual bar/area-chart sense; instead it uses **branching flows**.

## 3. Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Total water consumed (“1.9 trillion gallons of water”) | Quantitative | Overall total indicated by title text; implied by full combined flow area |
| Major water-use category (Livestock, Other crops, Everything else) | Categorical/nominal | Separate flow branches/segments; text labels |
| Subcategory within major category (Cotton, Wheat, Corn grain, Barley, Other crops, Thermoelectric power, Commercial and industrial, Residential) | Categorical/nominal | Nested flow branches; text labels |
| Share of total water use (percent values such as 56%, 24%, 21%, 12%, 7%, etc.) | Quantitative | Flow width/area; percentage labels |
| Water volume in gallons (e.g., 1,064 billion gallons; 448 billion gallons; 387 billion gallons) | Quantitative | Text labels for major categories |
| Hierarchical relationship / grouping (subcategory belonging to a major category) | Ordinal/structural grouping | Branching/nesting of flows from parent category |

## 2. Layout techniques
- Uses **flow bands** whose **width represents quantity/share**.

- No faceting or small multiples.
- Not stacked in the usual bar/area-chart sense; instead it uses **branching flows**.

|---|---|---|
| Total water consumed (“1.9 trillion gallons of water”) | Quantitative | Overall total indicated by title text; implied by full combined flow area |
| Major water-use category (Livestock, Other crops, Everything else) | Categorical/nominal | Separate flow branches/segments; text labels |
| Subcategory within major category (Cotton, Wheat, Corn grain, Barley, Other crops, Thermoelectric power, Commercial and industrial, Residential) | Categorical/nominal | Nested flow branches; text labels |
| Share of total water use (percent values such as 56%, 24%, 21%, 12%, 7%, etc.) | Quantitative | Flow width/area; percentage labels |
| Water volume in gallons (e.g., 1,064 billion gallons; 448 billion gallons; 387 billion gallons) | Quantitative | Text labels for major categories |
| Hierarchical relationship / grouping (subcategory belonging to a major category) | Ordinal/structural grouping | Branching/nesting of flows from parent category |

This graph shows how many gallons of water various categories consume from the Colorado River. The Colorado River, containing 1.9 trillion gallons of water, is an imperative source to fuel everyday life for millions of people. Of the annual consummtion average, 56% (1,064 bil gal) is consumed by livestock, 24% (448 bil gal) is consumed by a multitude of crops, and 21%(387 bil gal) is consumed by electricity, industrial, or residential use. In recent years, the river has dropped to one-third of its normal size. This has been linkedmto population growth and climate change. I wonder which more of an impact. Climate change is rapid and has affected ecosystems all around the world. I wonder if overconsumption linked to increasing population has hurt the Colorado River more than climate change. If the river’s flow rate proceeds to drop,will it remain a sustainable source? If not, I wonder how it will affect the surrounding communities. If it is to affect industrial companies, this could impact the American economy as a whole. In my own community, my county has two sustainable sources of water from rivers. However, we have experienced the wettest year to date but the driest October in over 100 years. This has made it difficult for farmers, who occupy most of the land, to maintain strong crops. While we have not dealt with decreasing access to river water supply, climate change’s impact on rainfall has hurt a main source of trade and income.

“As It Flows, Where Must Our Water Go?”

image_description:
## 1. Chart type
- **Alluvial / Sankey-style flow chart** showing how total water consumption is divided into categories and subcategories.

## 2. Layout techniques
- Uses **flow bands** whose **width represents quantity/share**.
- Shows **hierarchical splitting** from a total into major categories, then into subcategories.
- No faceting or small multiples.
- Not stacked in the usual bar/area-chart sense; instead it uses **branching flows**.

## 3. Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Total water consumed (“1.9 trillion gallons of water”) | Quantitative | Overall total indicated by title text; implied by full combined flow area |
| Major water-use category (Livestock, Other crops, Everything else) | Categorical/nominal | Separate flow branches/segments; text labels |
| Subcategory within major category (Cotton, Wheat, Corn grain, Barley, Other crops, Thermoelectric power, Commercial and industrial, Residential) | Categorical/nominal | Nested flow branches; text labels |
| Share of total water use (percent values such as 56%, 24%, 21%, 12%, 7%, etc.) | Quantitative | Flow width/area; percentage labels |
| Water volume in gallons (e.g., 1,064 billion gallons; 448 billion gallons; 387 billion gallons) | Quantitative | Text labels for major categories |
| Hierarchical relationship / grouping (subcategory belonging to a major category) | Ordinal/structural grouping | Branching/nesting of flows from parent category |
raw_comment: In this graph, it is showing that 1.9 trillion gallons of water from the Colorado River basin are being consumed in a typical year and splitting that consumption amount into three different categories: Livestock, Other Crops, and Everything else. I notice that the livestock has the greatest amount of consumption out of the three categories with it being 56% of the total amount consumed. I also noticed that cotton has the greatest consumption percentage compared to the other crops and think this is because producing cotton requires a very large amount of water compared to grain and other crops. I was surprised that only 12% of consumption was due to residential use and think that maybe this is because the Colorado River basin might not be zoned to many residential areas or it might be difficult to filter the water for drinking or other residential uses. I also wonder why the livestock consumption percentage is so high and think a possible reason could be that if there is a large amount of livestock near the Colorado River, that water is very accessible and useful for livestock drinking water and also crop irrigation. This relates to my community because even though I don’t live near the Colorado River, it is important to try to limit my daily water consumption as much as possible to help with problems like these. My headline for this graph would be: “With Record High Water Consumption, Will the Colorado River Remain?”

## 1. Chart type
- **Alluvial / Sankey-style flow chart** showing how total water consumption is divided into categories and subcategories.

## 2. Layout techniques
- Uses **flow bands** whose **width represents quantity/share**.
- Shows **hierarchical splitting** from a total into major categories, then into subcategories.
- No faceting or small multiples.
- Not stacked in the usual bar/area-chart sense; instead it uses **branching flows**.

## 3. Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Total water consumed (“1.9 trillion gallons of water”) | Quantitative | Overall total indicated by title text; implied by full combined flow area |
| Major water-use category (Livestock, Other crops, Everything else) | Categorical/nominal | Separate flow branches/segments; text labels |
| Subcategory within major category (Cotton, Wheat, Corn grain, Barley, Other crops, Thermoelectric power, Commercial and industrial, Residential) | Categorical/nominal | Nested flow branches; text labels |
| Share of total water use (percent values such as 56%, 24%, 21%, 12%, 7%, etc.) | Quantitative | Flow width/area; percentage labels |
| Water volume in gallons (e.g., 1,064 billion gallons; 448 billion gallons; 387 billion gallons) | Quantitative | Text labels for major categories |
| Hierarchical relationship / grouping (subcategory belonging to a major category) | Ordinal/structural grouping | Branching/nesting of flows from parent category |

## 1. Chart type
- **Alluvial / Sankey-style flow chart** showing how total water consumption is divided into categories and subcategories.

## 2. Layout techniques
- Uses **flow bands** whose **width represents quantity/share**.
- Shows **hierarchical splitting** from a total into major categories, then into subcategories.
- No faceting or small multiples.
- Not stacked in the usual bar/area-chart sense; instead it uses **branching flows**.

## 3. Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Total water consumed (“1.9 trillion gallons of water”) | Quantitative | Overall total indicated by title text; implied by full combined flow area |
| Major water-use category (Livestock, Other crops, Everything else) | Categorical/nominal | Separate flow branches/segments; text labels |
| Subcategory within major category (Cotton, Wheat, Corn grain, Barley, Other crops, Thermoelectric power, Commercial and industrial, Residential) | Categorical/nominal | Nested flow branches; text labels |
| Share of total water use (percent values such as 56%, 24%, 21%, 12%, 7%, etc.) | Quantitative | Flow width/area; percentage labels |
| Water volume in gallons (e.g., 1,064 billion gallons; 448 billion gallons; 387 billion gallons) | Quantitative | Text labels for major categories |
| Hierarchical relationship / grouping (subcategory belonging to a major category) | Ordinal/structural grouping | Branching/nesting of flows from parent category |

image_description:
## 1. Chart type
- **Alluvial / Sankey-style flow chart** showing how total water consumption is divided into categories and subcategories.

## 2. Layout techniques
- Uses **flow bands** whose **width represents quantity/share**.
- Shows **hierarchical splitting** from a total into major categories, then into subcategories.
- No faceting or small multiples.
- Not stacked in the usual bar/area-chart sense; instead it uses **branching flows**.

## 3. Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Total water consumed (“1.9 trillion gallons of water”) | Quantitative | Overall total indicated by title text; implied by full combined flow area |
| Major water-use category (Livestock, Other crops, Everything else) | Categorical/nominal | Separate flow branches/segments; text labels |
| Subcategory within major category (Cotton, Wheat, Corn grain, Barley, Other crops, Thermoelectric power, Commercial and industrial, Residential) | Categorical/nominal | Nested flow branches; text labels |
| Share of total water use (percent values such as 56%, 24%, 21%, 12%, 7%, etc.) | Quantitative | Flow width/area; percentage labels |
| Water volume in gallons (e.g., 1,064 billion gallons; 448 billion gallons; 387 billion gallons) | Quantitative | Text labels for major categories |
| Hierarchical relationship / grouping (subcategory belonging to a major category) | Ordinal/structural grouping | Branching/nesting of flows from parent category |

What I Notice:
I notice that 1.9 trillion gallons of water is consumed within the Colorado River Basin in a typical year. This information shocked me as I did not know that that much water was used from this river. I notice that livestock use most of the water (56%). Also, how cotton uses more water than wheat, corn grain, barley, and other crops.

What I Wonder:
Why does livestock consume most of the water? Why has climate change dropped the Colorado River Basin’s flow? What other uses does water provide to the world? Why does cotton use more water than wheat, corn grain, barley, and other crops? What renewable sources of energy can help protect water and supposedly replace it? How much of the water is consumed by humans? What is causing the Colorado River to dry up so quickly?

How This Relates to Me and My Community: 
This relates to me and my community because humans use a lot of water. The Colorado River “supplies drinking water to 40 million Americans in seven Western states.” This shows that this river provides people in the United States with a crucial water source. Without it, we would not be able to survive. Furthermore, in order to protect this water, we must not waste it and prevent it from becoming polluted. Water makes up 70% of the human body, which is why, without it, we would die. Also, only 1.2 percent of Earth's water can be consumed by humans which is why we must use it wisely.

Title: The River-ting Graph of the Consumption of the Colorado Basin.

## 1. Chart type
- **Alluvial / Sankey-style flow chart** showing how total water consumption is divided into categories and subcategories.

## 2. Layout techniques
- Uses **flow bands** whose **width represents quantity/share**.
- Shows **hierarchical splitting** from a total into major categories, then into subcategories.
- No faceting or small multiples.
- Not stacked in the usual bar/area-chart sense; instead it uses **branching flows**.

## 3. Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Total water consumed (“1.9 trillion gallons of water”) | Quantitative | Overall total indicated by title text; implied by full combined flow area |
| Major water-use category (Livestock, Other crops, Everything else) | Categorical/nominal | Separate flow branches/segments; text labels |
| Subcategory within major category (Cotton, Wheat, Corn grain, Barley, Other crops, Thermoelectric power, Commercial and industrial, Residential) | Categorical/nominal | Nested flow branches; text labels |
| Share of total water use (percent values such as 56%, 24%, 21%, 12%, 7%, etc.) | Quantitative | Flow width/area; percentage labels |
| Water volume in gallons (e.g., 1,064 billion gallons; 448 billion gallons; 387 billion gallons) | Quantitative | Text labels for major categories |
| Hierarchical relationship / grouping (subcategory belonging to a major category) | Ordinal/structural grouping | Branching/nesting of flows from parent category |

|---|---|---|

## 1. Chart type
- **Alluvial / Sankey-style flow chart** showing how total water consumption is divided into categories and subcategories.

## 2. Layout techniques
- Uses **flow bands** whose **width represents quantity/share**.
- Shows **hierarchical splitting** from a total into major categories, then into subcategories.
- No faceting or small multiples.
- Not stacked in the usual bar/area-chart sense; instead it uses **branching flows**.

## 3. Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Total water consumed (“1.9 trillion gallons of water”) | Quantitative | Overall total indicated by title text; implied by full combined flow area |
| Major water-use category (Livestock, Other crops, Everything else) | Categorical/nominal | Separate flow branches/segments; text labels |
| Subcategory within major category (Cotton, Wheat, Corn grain, Barley, Other crops, Thermoelectric power, Commercial and industrial, Residential) | Categorical/nominal | Nested flow branches; text labels |
| Share of total water use (percent values such as 56%, 24%, 21%, 12%, 7%, etc.) | Quantitative | Flow width/area; percentage labels |
| Water volume in gallons (e.g., 1,064 billion gallons; 448 billion gallons; 387 billion gallons) | Quantitative | Text labels for major categories |
| Hierarchical relationship / grouping (subcategory belonging to a major category) | Ordinal/structural grouping | Branching/nesting of flows from parent category |

image_description:
## 1. Chart type
- **Alluvial / Sankey-style flow chart** showing how total water consumption is divided into categories and subcategories.

## 2. Layout techniques
- Uses **flow bands** whose **width represents quantity/share**.
- Shows **hierarchical splitting** from a total into major categories, then into subcategories.
- No faceting or small multiples.
- Not stacked in the usual bar/area-chart sense; instead it uses **branching flows**.

## 3. Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Total water consumed (“1.9 trillion gallons of water”) | Quantitative | Overall total indicated by title text; implied by full combined flow area |
| Major water-use category (Livestock, Other crops, Everything else) | Categorical/nominal | Separate flow branches/segments; text labels |
| Subcategory within major category (Cotton, Wheat, Corn grain, Barley, Other crops, Thermoelectric power, Commercial and industrial, Residential) | Categorical/nominal | Nested flow branches; text labels |
| Share of total water use (percent values such as 56%, 24%, 21%, 12%, 7%, etc.) | Quantitative | Flow width/area; percentage labels |
| Water volume in gallons (e.g., 1,064 billion gallons; 448 billion gallons; 387 billion gallons) | Quantitative | Text labels for major categories |
| Hierarchical relationship / grouping (subcategory belonging to a major category) | Ordinal/structural grouping | Branching/nesting of flows from parent category |

## 1. Chart type
- **Alluvial / Sankey-style flow chart** showing how total water consumption is divided into categories and subcategories.

## 2. Layout techniques
- Uses **flow bands** whose **width represents quantity/share**.
- Shows **hierarchical splitting** from a total into major categories, then into subcategories.
- No faceting or small multiples.
- Not stacked in the usual bar/area-chart sense; instead it uses **branching flows**.

## 3. Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Total water consumed (“1.9 trillion gallons of water”) | Quantitative | Overall total indicated by title text; implied by full combined flow area |
| Major water-use category (Livestock, Other crops, Everything else) | Categorical/nominal | Separate flow branches/segments; text labels |
| Subcategory within major category (Cotton, Wheat, Corn grain, Barley, Other crops, Thermoelectric power, Commercial and industrial, Residential) | Categorical/nominal | Nested flow branches; text labels |
| Share of total water use (percent values such as 56%, 24%, 21%, 12%, 7%, etc.) | Quantitative | Flow width/area; percentage labels |
| Water volume in gallons (e.g., 1,064 billion gallons; 448 billion gallons; 387 billion gallons) | Quantitative | Text labels for major categories |
| Hierarchical relationship / grouping (subcategory belonging to a major category) | Ordinal/structural grouping | Branching/nesting of flows from parent category |

image_description:
## 1. Chart type
- **Alluvial / Sankey-style flow chart** showing how total water consumption is divided into categories and subcategories.

## 2. Layout techniques
- Uses **flow bands** whose **width represents quantity/share**.
- Shows **hierarchical splitting** from a total into major categories, then into subcategories.
- No faceting or small multiples.
- Not stacked in the usual bar/area-chart sense; instead it uses **branching flows**.

## 3. Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Total water consumed (“1.9 trillion gallons of water”) | Quantitative | Overall total indicated by title text; implied by full combined flow area |
| Major water-use category (Livestock, Other crops, Everything else) | Categorical/nominal | Separate flow branches/segments; text labels |
| Subcategory within major category (Cotton, Wheat, Corn grain, Barley, Other crops, Thermoelectric power, Commercial and industrial, Residential) | Categorical/nominal | Nested flow branches; text labels |
| Share of total water use (percent values such as 56%, 24%, 21%, 12%, 7%, etc.) | Quantitative | Flow width/area; percentage labels |
| Water volume in gallons (e.g., 1,064 billion gallons; 448 billion gallons; 387 billion gallons) | Quantitative | Text labels for major categories |
| Hierarchical relationship / grouping (subcategory belonging to a major category) | Ordinal/structural grouping | Branching/nesting of flows from parent category |

image_description:
## 1. Chart type
- **Alluvial / Sankey-style flow chart** showing how total water consumption is divided into categories and subcategories.

## 2. Layout techniques
- Uses **flow bands** whose **width represents quantity/share**.
- Shows **hierarchical splitting** from a total into major categories, then into subcategories.
- No faceting or small multiples.
- Not stacked in the usual bar/area-chart sense; instead it uses **branching flows**.

## 3. Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Total water consumed (“1.9 trillion gallons of water”) | Quantitative | Overall total indicated by title text; implied by full combined flow area |
| Major water-use category (Livestock, Other crops, Everything else) | Categorical/nominal | Separate flow branches/segments; text labels |
| Subcategory within major category (Cotton, Wheat, Corn grain, Barley, Other crops, Thermoelectric power, Commercial and industrial, Residential) | Categorical/nominal | Nested flow branches; text labels |
| Share of total water use (percent values such as 56%, 24%, 21%, 12%, 7%, etc.) | Quantitative | Flow width/area; percentage labels |
| Water volume in gallons (e.g., 1,064 billion gallons; 448 billion gallons; 387 billion gallons) | Quantitative | Text labels for major categories |
| Hierarchical relationship / grouping (subcategory belonging to a major category) | Ordinal/structural grouping | Branching/nesting of flows from parent category |

## 1. Chart type

## 2. Layout techniques
- Uses **flow bands** whose **width represents quantity/share**.
- Shows **hierarchical splitting** from a total into major categories, then into subcategories.
- No faceting or small multiples.
- Not stacked in the usual bar/area-chart sense; instead it uses **branching flows**.

## 3. Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Total water consumed (“1.9 trillion gallons of water”) | Quantitative | Overall total indicated by title text; implied by full combined flow area |
| Major water-use category (Livestock, Other crops, Everything else) | Categorical/nominal | Separate flow branches/segments; text labels |
| Subcategory within major category (Cotton, Wheat, Corn grain, Barley, Other crops, Thermoelectric power, Commercial and industrial, Residential) | Categorical/nominal | Nested flow branches; text labels |
| Share of total water use (percent values such as 56%, 24%, 21%, 12%, 7%, etc.) | Quantitative | Flow width/area; percentage labels |
| Water volume in gallons (e.g., 1,064 billion gallons; 448 billion gallons; 387 billion gallons) | Quantitative | Text labels for major categories |
| Hierarchical relationship / grouping (subcategory belonging to a major category) | Ordinal/structural grouping | Branching/nesting of flows from parent category |

|---|---|---|

| Water volume in gallons (e.g., 1,064 billion gallons; 448 billion gallons; 387 billion gallons) | Quantitative | Text labels for major categories |

4. It May Be Time For Meatless Monday
